Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 7 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Following affordability calculation, claimant proposes settlement agreement, and defendant accepts the settlement agreement

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42D-(1) This paragraph applies, if, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (i) it proposes a settlement agreement to the defendant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (ii) the settlement agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (iii) the settlement agreement if for repayment of the amount admitted in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) the defendant has, within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, used the OCMC website to notify the court that they have accepted the proposal and agree to the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) If the defendant has accepted the settlement agreement in those circumstances, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (3) When it stays the proceedings, the court must enable the claimant to return to court to request judgment on admission for any money still owed under the settlement agreement, if the settlement agreement breaks down and the defendant fails to comply with the settlement agreement. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4) If the settlement agreement breaks down, the claimant requests judgment on admission by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (6) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (7) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the terms of the settlement agreement, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (8) If a repayment date specified in the settlement agreement has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that settlement agreement, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) if the settlement agreement states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) if the settlement agreement states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Following affordability calculation, claimant proposes settlement agreement, but defendant rejects the settlement agreement, or fails to respond

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42E-(1) This paragraph applies if, after an affordability calculation has been done and the court has asked the claimant how they wish to proceed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (i) it proposes a settlement agreement to the defendant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (ii) the settlement agreement is in the form of OCON Settlement Agreement A; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (iii) the settlement agreement if for repayment of the amount admitted in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) within 7 days of the date of the claimant’s proposal, the defendant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they reject to the settlement agreement or the defendant does not respond to the court within the 7 days. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) If the defendant has rejected the settlement agreement or failed to respond within the 7 days in those circumstances, the claimant can request judgment on admission, by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5) The judgment must state that the amount is to be paid in accordance with the affordability calculation repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5A) If a repayment date specified in the affordability calculation repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment, and with subsequent instalments to be paid at one calendar month intervals after that. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (6) If, after the judgment has been made, the claimant changes their mind about the affordability calculation repayment plan and wishes to object to the plan, or the defendant wishes to object to the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination by a judge of the plan for the repayment of the amount admitted by the defendant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (7) The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court, by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the affordability calculation repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (8) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (9) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of OCMC to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Claimant rejects defendant’s proposed repayment plan, and also rejects affordability calculation repayment plan – judgment with repayment plan to be determined

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] 7.42F-(1) If, following an affordability calculation, the claimant wishes to reject the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may do so using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (2) If the claimant rejects the affordability calculation repayment plan, they may still request judgment on admission, by completing form OCON225 and submitting it to the court using the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment on admission, it must “enter judgment” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (4) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (a) the amount admitted;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (b) any interest on the amount admitted that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (c) court fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] minus any payments of the amount admitted on the response form (as defined) that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (5) The judgment must state that the plan for the repayment of the amount admitted by the defendant is to be determined. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (6) The plan for the repayment of the amount admitted by the defendant must be ordered by a judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (7) If either party objects to the plan for repayment ordered by the judge, they may ask, on time, for a redetermination of the plan for the repayment of the amount admitted by the defendant. The claimant or defendant may make their request for redetermination to the court, by email to the OCMC email address, or on paper to the OCMC postal address (as defined). When requesting a redetermination, the claimant or defendant must explain why they object to the plan ordered by the judge. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (8) The request for redetermination will be submitted to the court on time if it is received by the court within 19 days after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] (9) If the court receives a request for redetermination on time, it must send the claim out of OCMC to the defendant’s “home court” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42 The claimant accepts the part admission but not the repayment plan] Claimant rejects the defendant’s proposed repayment plan, proposes different terms – defendant is not an individual

## 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –] (a) the defendant is not an individual; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –] (b) the claimant has accepted the defendant’s offer, but has rejected the defendant’s proposed repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –] (2) The claimant may also suggest a repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –] (3) On receiving the claimant’s rejection, the court will send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, to the “CNBC” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.42G-(1) This paragraph applies where –] The claimant rejects the part admission

## 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (a)  where none of the parties is represented by a legal representative, the defendant’s response will be treated as a defence of the whole and the relevant provisions of Section 6 apply;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (b)  where all the parties are represented by a legal representative, or the claimant is represented by a legal representative but the defendant is not, the relevant  provisions of Section 6A apply, and the court must inform the parties of this. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] The claimant fails to respond to the part admission

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] 7.44 If, within 33 days after being asked by the court how they will respond to the defendant’s part admission and part defence or the defendant’s proposed repayment plan or (where relevant) affordability calculation repayment plan, the claimant fails to respond, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). If the claimant then responds later, the court must automatically “lift” the stay (as defined) to allow the proceedings to be resumed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] Sub-section E – Full and part admission – change of circumstances

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] 7.45 Full and part admission – circumstances change so that either party wants to change the repayment plan

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (1) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (a) there has been a judgment on admission or part admission;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (b) any (19-day) initial period for requesting redetermination of the repayment plan has ended; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (c) there has been a change of circumstances,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] either party may apply to the court to change the repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (2) A party makes an application to change a repayment plan by completing the relevant form set out in the table A, and submitting it to the court. (Sub-paragraph (3) explains what plan would be considered more favourable to a defendant.)

On receipt of the form, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (3) A more favourable plan would be one that required repayment of a lump sum to be made later, or by instalments. A more favourable plan would also be one that required repayment by smaller instalments than originally required. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] 7.46(1) If the defendant changes their mind and wants to withdraw their full or part admission, they may ask the court’s permission to withdraw the admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] ( 2) The defendant asks permission to withdraw their admission by making an application. (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (3) If the court receives an application for permission to withdraw, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.43 If the claimant rejects the part admission and wishes to continue with the claim –] (4) When the court sends the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims, it must direct that paragraph 7.2 of Civil Procedure Rule Practice Direction 14 is to apply to the application for permission to withdraw. That paragraph sets out the circumstances that the court has to consider, when it decides whether to give permission for a defendant to withdraw an admission that they made under Part 14 of the Civil Procedure Rules. ## Sub-section F – Admission submitted electronically, but not using the admission response screens

## 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (a) responding electronically to the court on time;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (b) admitting the whole or part of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (c) but not using the admission response screens on the OCMC website to make the whole or part admission; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (d) making no other response. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (2) When the court tells the claimant that it has received an informal admission, it must also send a copy of the informal admission to the claimant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (3) The claimant may request judgment on admission by completing and sending to the court form N225. Any such request must be supported by a copy of the informal admission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] (4) If the court receives a request for judgment on whole or part admission, it must refer the request to a judge for “directions” (as defined). The directions may include a direction to enter judgment, or a direction to send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.47(1) This sub-section applies if the defendant makes an “informal admission” by–] Sub-section G – multi-party claims over £25,000 where defendants’ responses differ

## 7.48(1) This sub-section applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.48(1) This sub-section applies where –] (a) the amount of the claim excluding interest is more than £25,000;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.48(1) This sub-section applies where –] (b) all the parties are represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.48(1) This sub-section applies where –] (c) there is more than one defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 7.48(1) This sub-section applies where –] (d) the defendants’ responses differ from one another. (2) Where this sub-section applies, on receipt of the last response, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the CNBC. ## SECTION 8 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE ONLINE – DEFENDANT COUNTERCLAIMS

## SECTION 9 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE UNDER PARAGRAPH 5.1 TABLE A USING FORM N9B – ALTERNATIVE RESPONSES

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 9 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE UNDER PARAGRAPH 5.1 TABLE A USING FORM N9B – ALTERNATIVE RESPONSES] Defendant’s response under paragraph 5.1 Table A using form N9B – alternative responses

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 9 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE UNDER PARAGRAPH 5.1 TABLE A USING FORM N9B – ALTERNATIVE RESPONSES] 9.1(1) Sub-paragraph (2) applies if, under paragraph 5.1 Table A, the defendant uses form N9B to make their response. Such a response is referred to as an “alternative response”. An example of alternative response is where the defendant counterclaims or brings another additional claim under Part 20 of the Civil Procedure Rules. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 9 – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE UNDER PARAGRAPH 5.1 TABLE A USING FORM N9B – ALTERNATIVE RESPONSES] 9.1(2) If the court receives an alternative response, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the CNBC. ## SECTION 10 – DEFENDANT ACTING IN PERSON – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE ON PAPER
